text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Australia's A$15 billion listed property trust industry, which has hit its highest level in more than a year and yesterday helped push the All Ords Index 24.3 points higher to 2,339.8, is set to double its gearing as it moves to take advantage of the slide in interest rates. Page 1.

National Mutual has joined Melbourne City Council in a consortium bidding for Tullamarine with plans to secure a stake of 20 to 25 percent in the Melbourne airport. National Mutual's partners in Victorian Airports Ltd include Pratt Industries and the preiously announced grouping of Macquarie Corporate Finance, Manchester Airport and the British contractor Serco Group Plc. Page 2.

Following the purchase of exclusive rights to a software package which allows growers to benchmark their performance against the district, wool broker Victorian Producers Cooperative Ltd has set a goal of reaching 20 percent of the market in south-eastern Australia. Page 5.

As the local market becomes increasingly undercut by foreign importers, appliance manufacturer Email Ltd wants to export more whitegoods to Asia. Email Ltd has an exclusive licence agreement with Electrolux which will underpin the company's goal of selling more products. Page 21.

Breakwater Island Trust , which is 32.23 owned by Jupiters, has only operated its own Keno game at the Townsville casino, but has the right to extend beyond the casino boundary to a 400 kilometre radius - meaning it holds the key to Jupiters' plans to opeate a Queensland-wide Keno game. Breakwater will ask unit holders next week to agree to surrender its North Queensland rights to Jupiters for A$500,000 and a 10-year, two per cent royalty. Page 19.

The long-awaited merger between Golden Shamrock Mines Ltd and London-based Ashanti Goldfields, in which 22.5 GSM shares will be exchanged for one Ashanti share plus additional cash payments for five-year periods, received shareholder approval at a meeting in Melbourne yesterday. Page 19.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In the most dramatic manifestation to date of BHP's internal review of its struggling steel business, the company has threatened to withdraw from raw steel production in New Zealand unless "a minimum" of 400 jobs can be cut at its Glenbrook steel mill nea Auckland. Page 19.

As the Wallis inquiry looks at regulation of the financial sector, the regional banks have stepped up their battle for survival by producing a survey - conducted by AGB McNair for Bank of Melbourne Ltd, Bendigo Bank Ltd and St George Bank Ltd - which indicates consumers believe banking takeovers will lead to decreased competition. Page 19.

The Australian Securities Commission has taken legal action to stop Marsford Investments Pte, the Singaporean subsidiary of Hong Kong-listed Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd, going ahead with its A$21.6 million Part C bid for Allied Queensland Coalfieds Ltd, claiming a breach of Australia's takeover laws. Page 21.

Bradmill Textiles, which last night won the Victorian Governor's export award for its high-quality denim, yesterday joined the growing number of textile and automotive manufacturers who are warning of disastrous consequences if the United States Governmen succeeds in forcing Australia to dump the export facilitation program. Page 21.

A special listing ceremony in Melbourne will mark the A$2.7 billion debut of heavyweight life insurer National Mutual Holdings NMH.AX on the Australian Stock Exchange today, where it will be one of the top 30 listed companies. The debut is at the head of an expected A$15 billion in insurance sector listings over the next three years. Page 21.

The stage is set for the West Australian Government to overrule the Murray Shire Council's extraordinary demand that giant French chemicals group Rhone Poulenc put up a A$10 million bond before approval is granted for a A$50 million investment in a rare earths plant at Pinjarra, south of Perth, due to concerns about possible long-term pollution. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Australian Securities Commission has asked Mail Boxes Etc, a business service centre in Mosman, for records of a private mail box rented by Mark Booth, the man at the centre of an investigation into trading in TNT stock during the lead-up to last weeks A$2 billion takeover bid by KPN. Page 25.

Industry sources close to Kerry Packer's Nine Network revealed yesterday Nine may be forced to arrange a special deal with Rupert Murdoch's News Limited if it decides to bid for the Super League free-to-air television rights because a Nine offer simply ivolving money would probably be rejected. Page 25.

In a run so strong the stock exchange asked the company whether there was any information not on the market, Whitegoods manufacturer Email's shares yesterday rose 10 cents to close at a 10-month high of A$3.50, with its market capitalisation jumping by moe than A$100 million in the past three trading days as investors rush to get positioned for the expected upturn of the housing market. Page 27.

The high-profile Victorian-based combination of the City of Melbourne Council, Pratt Group and National Mutual has allied itself with Macquarie Bank and other partners Manchester Airport and UK-based services company Serco to create a strong new contenderin the race for Melbourne Airport. Page 27.

Publishing and Broadcasting finance director Nick Falloon flew to the United States at the weekend to join Australis Media chairman Rod Price and finance director Geoff Kleemann to head up a roadshow for Australis, aimed at convincing US investors to partcipate in a A$189 million fund-raising. Page 27.

Australian Securities Commission spokesman Nigel Morris confirmed yesterday the ASC has launched a Federal Court action against Hong Kong-based Marsford Investments Pte Ltd, which launched a takeover bid for Allied Queensland Coalfields Ltd AWC.AX on September 2, on a possible breach of a 20 percent ownership ceiling in AQC. Page 27.
THE AGE

Linking up with two Victorian-based companies Pratt Group and National Mutual, Melbourne City Council will form the third part of a powerful contender in the bid for Melbourne Airport. The groups will contribute more than A$300 million to the bidding consrtium Victorian Airports Ltd and provide it with financial strength, operating skills and an understanding of the Melbourne economy. Page A1.

The sharemarket soared yesterday only marginally falling short of an all-time high. Small investors looked pleased as they were confident about future profits. The All Ordinaries closed at 2339.8, only 0.8 of a point off its February high. Page C1.

Victorian gas assets attracted another bidder yesterday when one of the world's biggest power distribution companies Pacific Gas and Electric declared itself in the game, claiming it would draw some heavy international bidding. Michael McDonald, managing irector of PG&E's subsidiary in Australia, PGT, predicted the Gas and Fuel would bring in a price well over A$1 billion. Page C3.

The title of Australia's biggest selling vehicle manufacturer could be returned to Holden which has remained at second or third place behind Ford and Toyota. Ford has claimed Holden has won back the title, helped by its popular Commodore, selling 5582 mor units than Ford's equivalent, the Falcon. With three months still to go, figures revealed the fight for the title is not over and the competition is close. Page C1.

While there have been claims employment is looking positive, reports have revealed unemployment is likely to rise above the nine percent mark early into next year. Chief economist for the ANZ Bank, Saul Eslake, said the number or job seekers was likely to exceed available work. He also said any hopes of an employment boost after the Budget had been dashed. Page C3.

In a move which will strengthen the feud between sugar producers Mackay Refined Sugars and CSR subsidiary New Zealand Sugar Corporation, Mackay will sue NZ Sugar Corp for A$8.9 million for allegedly misusing market power with the intention of eliminating ackay as a competitor in the refined-sugar market. The case, to be held in the New Zealand High Court, has caused valuable losses for both parties. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
